questions.text: Why should audio be low-pass filtered before downsampling?

options.A: To increase the number of amplitude levels available for each sample.
options.B: To prevent frequencies above the new Nyquist limit from aliasing.
options.C: To preserve every original frequency at the lower sampling rate.
options.D: To convert the waveform into frequency coefficients before storage.

questions.explanation: Downsampling lowers the Nyquist limit. Filtering out frequencies above that limit prevents them from folding into lower frequencies.

questions.text: A 7 kHz sine wave is sampled directly at 10 kHz without anti-alias filtering. At what frequency does its alias appear?
questions.explanation: The 7 kHz tone exceeds the 5 kHz Nyquist limit and folds to 10 − 7 = 3 kHz.

questions.text: For a DFT computed from N = 400 samples at sr = 16000, the dominant positive-frequency bin is k_star = 10. What does k_star * sr / N return?
questions.explanation: The bin spacing is 16000 / 400 = 40 Hz, so bin 10 corresponds to 400 Hz.
